questions.q: Why use the same seeds for both samplers?
options: The seed effect cancels within each pair, so fewer seeds are needed
It makes both pictures the same
questions.answer: The seed effect cancels within each pair, so fewer seeds are needed
questions.why: The lab: 8 seeds with pairs, 208 without, for the same range at our sizes.

questions.q: How much does quadrupling the seeds shrink the range?
Heun at 20 steps beats Euler at 20 steps. What is the fair next step?
options: Compare them at equal model calls
questions.answer: Compare them at equal model calls
questions.why: Heun spent 39 calls against 20. At about 20 calls each, the lab's table shows the real comparison.

questions.q: An SDE sampler's error from the exact ODE answer doesn't fall as steps rise. What's the correct reading?
options: That's the wrong measure for it, because it isn't following that ODE path
It is using the wrong seed
questions.answer: That's the wrong measure for it, because it isn't following that ODE path
questions.why: It draws fresh noise. Judge it with a measure that fits what it does.

questions.q: You test 15 samplers on 8 seeds and pick the best. What must you do before claiming it wins?
options: Test the winner again on new seeds
questions.answer: Test the winner again on new seeds
questions.why: Picking the best of many inflates it, even if all are equal, as the last line of the lab shows.

questions.q: The Sampling Lab renders all use one seed. What can they show?
options: How far a sampler moves one picture, and facts like two names giving the same pixels
questions.answer: How far a sampler moves one picture, and facts like two names giving the same pixels
questions.why: n = 1 can't rank anything, but it can reveal an exact match, because that's a fact about the code.
